docs.title: Script Reading Order — Top to Bottom!
The Golden Rule
docs.text:
Scratch ALWAYS reads blocks from TOP to BOTTOM in a script stack.

when green flag clicked        ← 1. FIRST
say [Hello!] for 2 secs        ← 2. SECOND
wait 1 secs                    ← 3. THIRD
move 100 steps                 ← 4. FOURTH
turn 90 degrees                ← 5. FIFTH

docs.title: Why Order Matters
docs.text: Wrong Order Result move 100 then say [Hello!] Moves FIRST, then speaks (awkward!) say [Hello!] then move 100 Speaks first, then moves (natural!)

docs.title: Parallel Scripts — Same Time!
docs.text:
Multiple scripts starting with the same hat block run SIMULTANEOUSLY!

when green flag clicked
forever
    move 5 steps
end

when green flag clicked
forever
    if <touching [edge v]?> then turn 180 degrees end
end

Both run at the same time — sprite moves AND checks edges at the same time!

docs.title: Parallelism — Doing Multiple Things at Once!
What Is Parallelism?
docs.text:
Parallelism = multiple scripts running at the same time.

In Scratch, every hat block starts a separate "thread" that runs independently.

docs.title: Examples of Parallelism
docs.text: Script 1 Script 2 Result Player movement (forever) Enemy patrol (forever) Both move at once! Animation (forever) Sensor check (forever) Smooth animation + collision detection Background music Gameplay loop Music plays while you play!

docs.title: Managing Parallelism
docs.text:
Challenge Solution Too many loops = lag Combine related code into ONE loop Race conditions Use broadcast and wait for coordination Conflicting changes Use variables to coordinate (e.g., game-state)

🧠 Think About Timing!

When two scripts might change the same variable, who runs first matters. Use broadcast and wait to control order!

docs.title: What Is a Boolean?
docs.text:
A Boolean is a value that can only be TRUE or FALSE — like a light switch!

Boolean Value Means True Yes, correct, on, 1 False No, incorrect, off, 0

docs.title: Boolean Blocks (Hexagon Shape ⬡)
docs.text: Block Category True When... touching [mouse-pointer v]? Sensing Sprite touches mouse key [space] pressed? Sensing Key held down touching [Sprite2 v]? Sensing Touching sprite < 10 > 5 > Operators 10 > 5 (true) < 3 = 5 > Operators 3 = 5 (false) < [score] > 100 > Operators Score > 100

docs.title: If-Else Structure (Review)
docs.text:
if <condition> then
    // TRUE path
else
    // FALSE path
end

docs.title: Boolean + If-Else = Smart Decisions!
docs.text:
if <touching [enemy v]?> then
    change lives by -1
    play sound [hurt v]
else
    // Safe! Keep playing
end

docs.title: Boolean Operators (And/Or/Not)
docs.text: Block What It Does Example < > and < > Both TRUE touching enemy AND lives > 0 < > or < > At least one touching spike OR touching lava not < > Flip it not touching ground (in air!)

docs.title: Key Pressed Block (Sensing)
docs.text:
key [space v] pressed?

True while key is held down, false when released.

docs.title: Common Keys for Games
docs.text: Key Typical Use right arrow Move right left arrow Move left up arrow / space Jump down arrow Duck / fall faster space Jump / shoot / interact a / d Alternative move keys w Jump (WASD controls)

docs.title: Smooth Movement Pattern (Best Practice!)
docs.text:
Don't use hat blocks for continuous movement! Use forever + if:

when green flag clicked
forever
    if <key [right arrow] pressed?> then
        change x by 5
        point in direction 90
        next costume
    end
    if <key [left arrow] pressed?> then
        change x by -5
        point in direction -90
        next costume
    end
    if <key [space] pressed?> then
        // Jump logic here
    end
end

Why? Hat blocks (when key pressed) only trigger once per press. forever + if checks every frame for smooth movement!

docs.title: Complete Player Controller
docs.text:
when green flag clicked
go to x: -200 y: -100
set rotation style [left-right v]
forever
    // Horizontal movement
    if <key [right arrow] pressed?> then
        change x by 5
        point in direction 90
        next costume
    end
    if <key [left arrow] pressed?> then
        change x by -5
        point in direction -90
        next costume
    end

    // Jump (simple)
    if <key [space] pressed?> and <touching [ground v]?> then
        repeat 15
            change y by 8
            wait 0.01 secs
        end
        repeat 15
            change y by -8
            wait 0.01 secs
        end
    end

    // Screen boundaries
    if < (x position) > 220 > then set x to 220 end
    if < (x position) < -220 > then set x to -220 end
end

docs.title: Key Concepts in This Controller
docs.text: Concept Implementation Smooth movement forever + if key pressed (not hat blocks) Facing direction point in direction 90 (right) / -90 (left) Animation next costume inside movement Ground check touching [ground v]? before jump Screen bounds Clamp X position to ±220

docs.title: Makey Makey Extension — Real World Controllers!
What Is Makey Makey?
docs.text:
Makey Makey is a circuit board that turns everyday objects into keyboard keys!

  • Bananas → arrow keys
  • Play-Doh → space bar
  • Aluminum foil → click
  • Your body → ground connection

docs.title: Adding Makey Makey
docs.text: Extensions → Makey Makey → Add → Makey Makey category (🟠 Orange)!

docs.title: Makey Makey Blocks
docs.text: Block What It Does when [key] pressed Works with Makey Makey keys when [clamped] connected Hat: object connected

docs.title: Makey Makey Ideas
docs.text:
Object Key Game Action Banana Right arrow Move right Banana Left arrow Move left Apple Space Jump Water cup Click Shoot Your hand (ground) — Completes circuit

🍌 Anything Conductive = Button!

Anything that conducts electricity can be a game controller — fruit, foil, pencil graphite, plants, people!

For precise collisions, use a small invisible "hitbox" sprite:

Forever:

    end

docs.title: What Is Event-Driven Programming?
docs.text: Code runs in response to events (clicks, key presses, broadcasts, sensor triggers) rather than running top-to-bottom once.

docs.title: Scratch Is Event-Driven!
docs.text: Event Hat Block Example Project starts when green flag clicked Initialize game Sprite clicked when this sprite clicked Buttons, collectibles Key pressed when [space] key pressed Jump, shoot Broadcast received when I receive [msg] Coordinated actions Backdrop changes when backdrop switches to Level transitions Video motion when video [motion] > 50 Camera games Clone created when I start as a clone Particle systems

docs.title: Benefits of Event-Driven
docs.text: Benefit Explanation Responsive Instant reaction to player input Efficient Code only runs when needed Modular Each script handles one event Natural for games Games are all about reacting!

docs.text:

docs.title: Key Terms to Remember

True while key held Player Control Movement + jump + bounds Makey Makey Physical objects as keys Collision Detection Detecting sprite/color/edge contact Less Than Operator < comparison go to x: y: Instant teleport glide secs to Smooth movement create clone Runtime sprite copy Event-Driven Code runs in response to events

docs.title: Greater Than Operator (>)
docs.text:
< (10) > (5) >

True if left number is BIGGER than right number.

Example Result 10 > 5 True ✅ 5 > 10 False ❌ 10 > 10 False ❌ (not greater, equal)

Use for: High score checks, boundary limits, "is big enough?"

docs.title: Equal Operator (=)
docs.text:
< (10) = (10) >

True if both numbers are EXACTLY the same.

Example Result 10 = 10 True ✅ 10 = 5 False ❌ 0 = 0 True ✅

Use for: Exact matches, "did we reach exactly 100?", "is timer 0?"

docs.title: All Three Comparison Operators
docs.text: Block Symbol True When... Memory Trick < > < Left SMALLER than right "Less than" points to smaller < > > Left BIGGER than right "Greater than" points to bigger < = > = Left EQUALS right Two lines = same

docs.title: Pick Random Block (Operators → Green)
docs.text:
pick random (1) to (10)

Gives a random whole number between the two numbers (including both!).

docs.title: Random Number Uses
docs.text: Code Range Use For pick random 1 to 6 1–6 Dice roll pick random 1 to 100 1–100 Percent chance (1% each) pick random -10 to 10 -10 to 10 Random direction pick random 0 to 360 0–360 Random angle

docs.title: Random Spawn Position
docs.text:
when I start as a clone
go to x: (pick random -200 to 200) y: (pick random -150 to 150)

docs.title: Random Chance (20% = 1 in 5)
docs.text:
if < (pick random 1 to 5) = 1 > then
    // 20% chance!
    broadcast [rare-item v]
end

docs.title: Random Wait
docs.text:
forever
    wait (pick random 1 to 3) secs
    create clone of [myself v]
end

docs.title: Repeat Block (Control → Orange)
docs.text:
repeat (10)
    move 10 steps
    turn 15 degrees
end

Runs exactly N times — perfect when you know how many!

docs.title: Draw a Polygon
docs.text:
repeat (5)        // Pentagon
    move 100 steps
    turn 72 degrees    // 360/5 = 72
end

docs.title: Spawn Exact Number
docs.text:
repeat (10)
    create clone of [myself v]
    wait 0.5 secs
end

docs.title: Countdown
docs.text:
set [countdown v] to (10)
repeat (10)
    say (countdown) for 1 secs
    change [countdown v] by (-1)
end

docs.title: What Is a Variable?
docs.text:
A variable is a named box that holds one value that can change.

set [score v] to (0)    // Put 0 in the "score" box
change [score v] by (10)  // Add 10 to the box

docs.title: Variable Blocks (Variables → Red)
docs.text: Block What It Does set [name v] to (value) Put exact value in box change [name v] by (amount) Add/subtract from box show variable [name] Display on stage hide variable [name] Remove from stage variable (reporter) Get current value

docs.title: Creating Variables
docs.text:
1. Click Variables (🔴 Red)
  2. Click Make a Variable
  3. Name it: score, lives, timer, level, high-score
  4. Choose scope:
  5. For all sprites = shared (one box for everyone)
  6. For this sprite only = private (each sprite has own)
  7. Click OK!

docs.title: Variable Scope — Who Can See It?
docs.text: Scope Who Sees It Use For For all sprites Everyone shares ONE box Score, timer, high score, level For this sprite only Each sprite has own box Player health, enemy speed, sprite state

docs.title: Score System
docs.text:
when green flag clicked
set [score v] to (0)
show variable [score v]

when I receive [coin-collected v]
change [score v] by (10)

docs.title: Lives System
docs.text:
when green flag clicked
set [lives v] to (3)
show variable [lives v]

when I receive [player-hit v]
change [lives v] by (-1)
if < (lives) = 0 > then
    broadcast [game-over v]
end

docs.title: Timer
docs.text:
when green flag clicked
set [timer v] to (0)
show variable [timer v]
forever
    wait (1) secs
    change [timer v] by (1)
end

docs.title: Show Variable
docs.text:
show variable [score v]

Displays the variable on the stage (top-left by default).

docs.title: Hide Variable
docs.text:
hide variable [score v]

Removes from stage — but value still exists!

docs.title: When to Show/Hide
docs.text:
Situation Action Game starts show variable [score], show variable [lives] Menu screen hide variable [score], show variable [high-score] Game over hide variable [lives], show variable [final-score] Pause menu hide variable [timer]

👁️ Show What Matters!

Only show variables the player needs to see right now. Too many = clutter!

docs.title: What Is a List?
docs.text:
A list is like a variable, but holds MULTIPLE values in order — like a shopping list!

List: inventory
[0] "sword"
[1] "shield"
[2] "potion"
[3] "key"

docs.title: Creating a List
docs.text:
1. Click Variables (🔴 Red)
  2. Click Make a List
  3. Name it: inventory, high-scores, level-codes, player-names
  4. Choose scope: For all sprites or For this sprite only
  5. Click OK!

docs.title: List Blocks (Variables → Dark Red)
docs.text: Block What It Does add [thing v] to [list v] Append to end delete (1) of [list v] Remove item at position insert [thing v] at (1) of [list v] Insert at position replace item (1) of [list v] with [thing v] Change existing item (1) of [list v] Reporter: get value at position length of [list v] Reporter: how many items list contains [thing v]? Boolean: is it in list? show list [name] Display on stage hide list [name] Hide from stage delete all of [list v] Clear everything

docs.title: Inventory System
docs.text:
when green flag clicked
delete all of [inventory v]
add [sword] to [inventory v]
add [shield] to [inventory v]
show list [inventory v]

when I receive [found-potion v]
add [potion] to [inventory v]

docs.title: High Score List
docs.text:
when green flag clicked
delete all of [high-scores v]
repeat 5
    add (0) to [high-scores v]
end

when I receive [new-score v]
if < (score) > (item (1) of [high-scores v]) > then
    insert (score) at (1) of [high-scores v]
    delete (6) of [high-scores v]  // Keep top 5
end

docs.title: What Are Parameters?
docs.text:
Parameters are inputs for your custom blocks — like function arguments!

define jump (height)
change y by (height)
wait 0.2 secs
change y by (height * -1)

Use it: jump (100) → jumps high! jump (20) → small hop!

docs.title: Adding Parameters
docs.text:
1. Make a Block in My Blocks (🩷 Pink)
  2. Click Options (gear icon)
  3. Click Add number input or Add string input
  4. Name it: height, speed, name, color
  5. Click OK — parameter appears in define hat!

docs.title: Parameter Types
docs.text: Type Accepts Example Use Number input Numbers jump (height), move (steps) String input Text say (message), set name to (name) Boolean input True/false if (condition) then

docs.title: Jump with Height
docs.text:
define jump (height)
change y by (height)
wait 0.2 secs
change y by (height * -1)

Use: jump (100) = high jump, jump (20) = small hop

docs.title: Draw Polygon
docs.text:
define polygon (sides) (size)
repeat (sides)
    move (size) steps
    turn (360 / sides) degrees
end

Use: polygon (5) (100) = pentagon, polygon (8) (50) = octagon!

docs.title: Glide to Position
docs.text:
define glide-to (target-x) (target-y) (seconds)
glide (seconds) secs to x: (target-x) y: (target-y)

Use: glide-to (100) (50) (2) — smooth move to (100, 50) in 2 secs!

docs.title: What Is Abstraction?
docs.text:
Abstraction = hiding complex details behind a simple name.

Analogy: You press "Start" on a microwave. You don't need to know how magnetrons work — you just press "Start"!

docs.title: In Scratch: Custom Blocks = Abstraction!
docs.text:
define draw-house (size)
repeat 4
    move (size) steps
    turn 90 degrees
end
move (size) steps
turn 30 degrees
repeat 3
    move (size) steps
    turn 120 degrees
end

User just types: draw-house (100) — doesn't need to know the math!

docs.title: Why Abstraction Helps
docs.text: Benefit Explanation Less repetition Write once, use many times Easier to read draw-house vs 20 motion blocks Easy to fix Change once, fixes everywhere Shareable Backpack your blocks to other projects

pen down      // Start drawing
move 100 steps

forever

docs.title: Accessibility Features — Making Games for Everyone!
Why Accessibility Matters
docs.text: Games should be fun for everyone — including players with different abilities!

docs.title: Project Description — What Are We Building?
The Big Picture
docs.text: Before writing code, we describe the project — like a movie pitch!

docs.title: Project Description Template
docs.text: Section What to Include Title Catchy name: "Space Runner 3000" Genre Platformer, puzzle, shooter, story Core Mechanic "Run, jump, collect stars, avoid spikes" Goal "Reach the end of 5 levels" Controls "Arrows move, Space jumps" Look & Feel "Retro pixel art, synthwave music"

docs.title: Example Project Description
docs.text:
Title: "Coin Collector Extreme" Genre: Platformer / Collection Core Mechanic: Run, jump, and dash through 10 levels collecting golden coins while avoiding enemies and spikes. Goal: Collect all 50 coins in each level to unlock the next. Beat all 5 worlds! Controls: Arrow keys move, Space jumps, Shift dashes. Look & Feel: Bright cartoon style, upbeat chiptune music, particle effects on coin collect.

📝 Write It Down First!

A clear project description keeps you focused and helps you explain your game to others!

docs.title: Algorithmic Thinking — Think Like a Computer!
What Is an Algorithm?
docs.text: An algorithm is a step-by-step recipe for solving a problem — precise enough that a computer can follow it!

docs.title: Algorithmic Thinking Steps
docs.text: Step Question Example 1. Understand What's the problem? "Make player jump realistically" 2. Break Down What are the steps? "Check ground → apply force → apply gravity → land" 3. Order What comes first? Check ground → if on ground & space → jump → apply gravity each frame 4. Test Does it work? Test jump height, double-jump prevention, landing 5. Improve Can it be better? Add coyote time, jump buffering, variable height

docs.title: Algorithmic Thinking in Scratch
docs.text: Thinking Step Scratch Translation Sequence Blocks top-to-bottom Condition if < > then else Loop repeat, forever, repeat until Variable score, timer, velocity Function Custom block (define jump)

docs.title: Costume Animation — Bring Sprites to Life!
How Animation Works
docs.text: Animation = rapidly switching costumes (pictures) to create illusion of movement!

docs.title: Animation Blocks (Looks → Purple)
docs.text: Block What It Does switch costume to [costume1 v] Instant change to specific costume next costume Cycle to next in list costume # Reporter: current costume number

docs.title: Smooth Animation Pattern
docs.text:
when green flag clicked
forever
    next costume
    wait 0.1 secs
end

Cycles through all costumes with a 0.1 sec delay between each!

docs.title: Animation Timing
docs.text: Wait Time Effect 0.05 secs Very fast (hummingbird wings) 0.1 secs Normal walk/run 0.2 secs Slow walk, heavy character 0.5 secs Very slow (zombie shuffle)

docs.title: Walking Animation (4 costumes: walk1, walk2, walk3, walk4)
docs.text:
when green flag clicked
forever
    if <key [right arrow] pressed?> then
        next costume
        wait 0.1 secs
    else
        switch costume to [idle v]
    end
end

docs.title: Flying Animation (2 costumes: wings-up, wings-down)
docs.text:
forever
    next costume
    wait 0.15 secs
end

docs.title: Attack Animation (3 frames: windup, strike, recovery)
docs.text:
when [space] key pressed
switch costume to [windup v]
wait 0.1 secs
switch costume to [strike v]
wait 0.05 secs
switch costume to [recovery v]
wait 0.1 secs
switch costume to [idle v]

docs.title: Costume Center Reminder!
docs.text: Set costume center to FEET for walking characters — prevents "floating" or "sinking" during animation!

docs.title: What Is Continuous Motion?
docs.text: Continuous motion = sprite moves smoothly every frame while key held, not in jumps!

docs.title: The Secret: Forever + If (Not Hat Blocks!)
❌ Wrong: Hat Blocks (Choppy!)
docs.text:
when [right arrow] key pressed
change x by 10

Only moves ONCE per key press! Choppy!

docs.title: ✅ Correct: Forever + If (Smooth!)
docs.text:
when green flag clicked
forever
    if <key [right arrow] pressed?> then
        change x by 5
        point in direction 90
        next costume
    end
    if <key [left arrow] pressed?> then
        change x by -5
        point in direction -90
        next costume
    end
end

Checks every frame — buttery smooth!

docs.title: Continuous Motion Template
docs.text:
when green flag clicked
forever
    // Horizontal
    if <key [right arrow] pressed?> then
        change x by (speed)
        point in direction 90
        next costume
    end
    if <key [left arrow] pressed?> then
        change x by (speed * -1)
        point in direction -90
        next costume
    end

    // Vertical (gravity, jump)
    // ... jump code here ...

    wait 0.01 secs    // Critical! Prevents lag
end

docs.title: Speed Variables
docs.text:
when green flag clicked
set [walk-speed v] to (5)
set [run-speed v] to (10)
set [jump-power v] to (15)

forever
    if <key [right arrow] pressed?> then
        change x by (walk-speed)
    end
    // ...
end

Easy to tweak! Change walk-speed variable to adjust feel.

docs.title: The Illusion of Movement
docs.text: Scrolling background = move background opposite to player = feels like player moves through big world!

docs.title: Method 1: Multiple Background Sprites
docs.text:
Background1 (original)
Background2 (copy, positioned right next to 1)

forever
    change x by (-scroll-speed)  // Move left
    if <x < -480> then
        go to x: 480   // Wrap to right side
    end
end

docs.title: Method 2: Backdrop Switching
docs.text:
forever
    if <player near edge> then
        next backdrop
        // Reposition everything for new scene
    end
end

docs.title: Scrolling Background Example
docs.text:
when green flag clicked
go to x: 0 y: 0
forever
    change x by (-3)    // Scroll left at speed 3
    if < (x position) < -480 > then
        go to x: 480     // Teleport to right side
    end
end

Two copies side-by-side = infinite seamless scroll!

docs.title: What Is Beat Sync?
docs.text: Beat synchronization = game actions happen on the musical beat!

docs.title: Using Tempo
docs.text:
when green flag clicked
forever
    wait (60 / tempo) secs    // One beat at current tempo
    // Do something on beat
    change color effect by 25
end

docs.title: Visual Beat
docs.text:
forever
    wait (60 / tempo) secs
    change size by 10
    wait 0.1 secs
    change size by -10
end

docs.title: Obstacle Spawn on Beat
docs.text:
forever
    wait (60 / tempo) secs
    if < (pick random 1 to 4) = 1 > then
        create clone of [obstacle v]
    end
end

docs.title: Music-Reactive Background
docs.text:
when green flag clicked
forever
    wait (60 / tempo) secs
    change color effect by 10
    change pen color by 5
end

🎵 Beat Sync = Rhythm Game!

Scratch's tempo variable (default 60 BPM) lets you sync everything to music!

docs.title: What Is Loop Nesting?
docs.text: Loop nesting = putting a loop inside another loop!

docs.title: Nested Loop Structure
docs.text:
repeat (outer)
    repeat (inner)
        // Do something many times
    end
end

Total iterations = outer × inner

docs.title: Grid Pattern (Rows × Columns)
docs.text:
repeat (5)          // 5 rows
    repeat (10)     // 10 columns
        stamp
        move 20 steps
    end
    go to x: -100 y: (y + 20)   // Next row
end

Creates 50 stamps in a 5×10 grid!

docs.title: Nested Animation
docs.text:
repeat (3)              // 3 waves
    repeat (10)         // 10 ripples per wave
        change size by 5
        wait 0.05 secs
    end
    repeat (10)
        change size by -5
        wait 0.05 secs
    end
end

docs.title: Spiral with Nested Loops
docs.text:
repeat (6)              // 6 arms
    repeat (60)         // 60 steps per arm
        move 5 steps
        turn 1 degrees
        change pen color by 1
    end
    turn 60 degrees     // Next arm
end

docs.title: Types of Enemy AI
docs.text: Type Behavior Code Pattern Patrol Back and forth repeat until edge, turn 180 Chase Follow player point towards player, move Random Wander randomly pick random direction, move Turret Stay put, shoot point towards player, shoot Boss Phases, patterns Broadcast + phases

docs.title: Patrol Enemy (Back and Forth)
docs.text:
when green flag clicked
forever
    move 3 steps
    if <touching [edge v]?> then
        turn 180 degrees
    end
end

docs.title: Chase Enemy
docs.text:
when green flag clicked
forever
    point towards [player v]
    move 2 steps
    if <touching [player v]?> then
        broadcast [player-hit v]
    end
end

docs.title: Smart Patrol (Platform Edges)
docs.text:
forever
    move 2 steps
    if <touching [edge v]?> or <not <touching color [#8B4513]?>> then
        turn 180 degrees
    end
end

Turns around at platform edges (brown color #8B4513 = ground)!

docs.title: Enemy Variations
docs.text: Variation Code Change Fast enemy move 5 steps instead of 2 Jumping enemy Add jump logic on timer Shooting enemy if <distance < 200> then broadcast [shoot] Boss Phases: broadcast [phase1], broadcast [phase2]

docs.title: Debugging Basics — Finding and Fixing Bugs!
What Is a Bug?
docs.text: A bug = code that doesn't do what you intended. Debugging = finding and fixing it!

docs.title: Debugging Steps
docs.text: Step Action 1. Reproduce Make the bug happen consistently 2. Isolate Find which script/block causes it 3. Hypothesize "I think the change x by is wrong" 4. Test Change one thing, test again 4. Fix Apply the correction 5. Verify Test thoroughly — did it fix? Any new bugs?

docs.title: Scratch Debugging Tools
docs.text: Tool How to Use Block Highlighting Watch which block glows when running Variable Watchers Show variables on stage — watch values live say for Debug say (variable) for 2 secs — prints value Single Step Click green flag, then press space to step (in some versions) wait for Timing Add wait 1 secs to slow down and watch

docs.title: Common Bugs & Fixes
docs.text: Bug Likely Cause Fix Sprite doesn't move Wrong hat block, or forever missing Check hat block, add forever Moves wrong direction change x by -10 vs 10 Check positive/negative Jumps forever No ground check Add touching ground? Stuck in wall No edge check Add touching color? check Score doesn't increase Wrong variable name Check spelling: score vs Score Infinite loop Missing wait in forever Add wait 0.01 secs

docs.title: Debugging with say
docs.text:
when green flag clicked
forever
    say (join [x: ] (x position)) for 0.1 secs
    // Shows x position live!
end

Live variable display — watch values change in real time!

docs.title: Broadcast vs Broadcast And Wait
docs.text: Block Behavior broadcast [msg] Sends, continues immediately broadcast [msg] and wait Sends, waits for ALL receivers

docs.title: When to Use Broadcast And Wait
docs.text: Use Case Why Level start All sprites ready before gameplay Cutscene steps Each phase completes before next Save game All data saved before continuing Level complete All effects finish before next level

docs.title: Broadcast And Wait Example
docs.text:
when green flag clicked
broadcast [setup-level v] and wait
wait 1 secs
broadcast [spawn-player v] and wait
broadcast [spawn-enemies v] and wait
broadcast [game-start v]

Each phase finishes completely before next starts!

docs.title: What Is Message Passing?
docs.text: Message passing = sprites communicating via broadcasts instead of directly accessing each other.

docs.title: Why Message Passing?
docs.text: Benefit Explanation Loose coupling Sprites don't need to know about each other Flexible Add/remove sprites without breaking others Scalable Add more sprites easily

docs.title: Message Passing Patterns
docs.text: Pattern Sender Receiver Use For Event broadcast [coin] when I receive [coin] Score +10 Command broadcast [jump] when I receive [jump] All sprites jump Query broadcast [get-score] when I receive [get-score] → broadcast [score-is] + wait Get data

docs.title: Broadcast (Fire and Forget)
docs.text:
broadcast [explosion v]
// Continues immediately!

Doesn't wait — sender continues instantly.

docs.title: When to Use Async Broadcast
docs.text: Situation Why Async Effects Explosion, particles — don't block gameplay Notifications "Achievement unlocked" — don't pause game Logging Send analytics — don't slow down

docs.title: Decision Making — If This, Then That!
Decision Making in Code
docs.text: Every game is a series of decisions: - Is player on ground? → Allow jump - Is score > 100? → Level up - Touching enemy? → Lose life - Timer = 0? → Game over

docs.title: Decision Blocks
docs.text: Block Use For if < > then One option if < > then else Two paths repeat until < > Loop until condition < > and < > Both must be true < > or < > Either true

docs.title: If-Else Review
docs.text:
if <condition> then
    // TRUE path
else
    // FALSE path
end

docs.title: Simple Branch
docs.text:
if <touching [coin v]?> then
    change score by 10
else
    // Nothing, keep playing
end

docs.title: Multi-Level Branch
docs.text:
if < (score) > 1000 > then
    broadcast [level-3 v]
else
    if < (score) > 500 > then
        broadcast [level-2 v]
    else
        broadcast [level-1 v]
    end
end

docs.title: When I Start As Clone — Clone Initialization!
Clone Hat Block
docs.text:
when I start as a clone

Runs automatically for EACH new clone — perfect for initialization!

docs.title: Clone Initialization Pattern
docs.text:
when I start as a clone
go to x: (pick random -200 to 200) y: (180)
set [velocity-y v] to (0)
show

forever
    change y by (velocity-y)
    change [velocity-y v] by (-1)   // Gravity
    if <touching [ground v]?> then
        delete this clone
    end
end

Every clone sets itself up automatically!

docs.title: Clone Initialization Checklist
docs.text: Step Code Position go to x: (random) y: (top) Variables set [velocity v] to (0) Appearance switch costume to [rock v], show Behavior forever { physics, check delete }

docs.title: What Are Concurrent Scripts?
docs.text: Concurrent scripts = multiple scripts running at the same time (parallelism).

docs.title: Scratch = Naturally Concurrent!
docs.text: Every hat block starts a new "thread" that runs independently.

docs.title: Managing Concurrency
docs.text: Challenge Solution Variable conflicts Use broadcast and wait for order Race conditions Single "manager" script for shared data Too many loops Combine into one main game loop

docs.title: Concurrency Example
docs.text:
when green flag clicked          // Script 1: Player
forever
    // Movement, jump, animation
end

when green flag clicked          // Script 2: Enemies
forever
    // Spawn, move, check collisions
end

when green flag clicked          // Script 3: UI
forever
    // Update score display, timer
end

All three run simultaneously!

docs.title: What Is Physical Computing?
docs.text: Physical computing = code interacting with real-world hardware (sensors, motors, lights)!

docs.title: Scratch Hardware Extensions
docs.text: Hardware Extension What It Does Makey Makey Makey Makey Everyday objects → keys micro:bit micro:bit Buttons, LEDs, accelerometer LEGO SPIKE LEGO® Motors, sensors, robots Go Direct Go Direct Science sensors (temp, force, etc.)

docs.title: Makey Makey Example
docs.text:
when [banana] key pressed
change x by 10

Banana = right arrow key!

docs.title: micro:bit Example
docs.text:
when [button A] pressed
change x by 10

when [tilt left] detected
turn 15 degrees

docs.title: Physical Computing Ideas
docs.text: Project Hardware Code Idea Fruit Piano Makey Makey Each fruit = note Tilt Maze micro:bit Tilt to roll ball Robot Dance LEGO SPIKE Code dance moves Weather Station Go Direct Log temp, graph it

docs.title: Repeat Until Block
docs.text:
repeat until <condition>
    // Runs until condition becomes TRUE
end

Checks condition at START of each iteration.

docs.title: Move Until Edge
docs.text:
repeat until <touching [edge v]?>
    move 5 steps
end

docs.title: Wait for Button
docs.text:
repeat until <key [space] pressed?>
    say [Press SPACE to start]
    wait 0.5 secs
end

docs.title: Wait for Condition
docs.text:
repeat until < (score) > 100 >
    wait 1 secs
end
broadcast [level-complete v]

docs.title: Repeat Until vs Other Loops
docs.text: Loop Type Stops When... repeat (10) After 10 iterations forever Never (until stop) repeat until <cond> Condition becomes TRUE

docs.title: Boolean Operators (Operators → Green)
docs.text: Block Symbol True When... < > and < > AND Both TRUE < > or < > OR At least one TRUE not < > NOT Flips TRUE↔FALSE

docs.title: AND — Both Must Be True
docs.text:
if <touching [coin v]?> and < (lives) > 0 > then
    change score by 10
end

docs.title: OR — At Least One
docs.text:
if <touching [spike v]?> or <touching [lava v]?> then
    broadcast [player-hit v]
end

docs.title: NOT — Flip It
docs.text:
if <not <touching [ground v]?>> then
    // In the air!
    change [velocity-y v] by (-1)   // Gravity
end

docs.title: Truth Tables
docs.text: A B A AND B A OR B NOT A T T T T F T F F T F F T F T T F F F F T

docs.title: Dice Roll = Pick Random 1 to 6
docs.text:
pick random (1) to (6)

Simulates a 6-sided die!

docs.title: Dice Roll Uses
docs.text: Code Simulates Use For pick random 1 to 6 1d6 Board games, RPGs pick random 1 to 20 1d20 D&D style (pick random 1 to 6) + (pick random 1 to 6) 2d6 Monopoly, Catan pick random 1 to 100 d100 Percentile rolls

docs.title: Attack Roll
docs.text:
if < (pick random 1 to 20) > 15 > then
    // Critical hit!
    change [damage v] by (10)
else
    change [damage v] by (5)
end

docs.title: Loot Table
docs.text:
set [roll v] to (pick random 1 to 100)
if < (roll) < 50 > then
    add [common-item] to [inventory v]
else
    if < (roll) < 80 > then
        add [uncommon-item] to [inventory v]
    else
        if < (roll) < 95 > then
            add [rare-item] to [inventory v]
        else
            add [legendary-item] to [inventory v]
        end
    end
end

docs.title: Change Variable — Math on the Fly!
Change Variable Block
docs.text:
change [score v] by (10)

Adds (or subtracts) from current value.

docs.title: Change Variable Patterns
docs.text: Code Effect change [score v] by (10) +10 change [score v] by (-5) -5 change [x v] by (10) Move right change [x v] by (-10) Move left change [velocity-y v] by (-1) Gravity!

docs.title: Score System
docs.text:
when I receive [coin v]
change [score v] by (10)

when I receive [gem v]
change [score v] by (50)

when I receive [boss-defeated v]
change [score v] by (1000)

docs.title: Physics Velocity
docs.text:
when green flag clicked
set [velocity-x v] to (0)
set [velocity-y v] to (0)
forever
    change [velocity-y v] by (-0.5)   // Gravity
    change x by (velocity-x)
    change y by (velocity-y)
end

docs.title: Cooldown Timer
docs.text:
when [space] key pressed
if < (cooldown) = 0 > then
    set [cooldown v] to (30)   // 30 frames = 0.5 sec at 60fps
    broadcast [shoot v]
end

forever
    if < (cooldown) > 0 > then
        change [cooldown v] by (-1)
    end
end

docs.title: Variable Scope — For All vs This Sprite!
For All Sprites (Global)
docs.text:
set [score v] to (0)    // ONE box, everyone shares

All sprites see and change the SAME value.

docs.title: For This Sprite Only (Local)
docs.text:
set [health v] to (100)    // EACH sprite has own box

Each sprite has its OWN private copy.

docs.title: When to Use Which
docs.text: Scope Use For Example For all sprites Shared game state score, timer, level, high-score For this sprite only Individual state health, speed, ammo, facing-right

docs.title: Scope Example
docs.text:
Player script:
set [score v] to (0)           // Global
set [player-health v] to (100) // Local

Enemy script:
when I start as a clone
set [enemy-health v] to (50)   // Local (each clone own!)

docs.title: Add To List Block
docs.text:
add [apple] to [inventory v]

Appends to END of list.

docs.title: Run Without Screen Refresh — Turbo Mode! ⚡
What Is "Run Without Screen Refresh"?

docs.text: Use Case Why Not Turbo Animations Player WON'T see movement! Visual effects Particles, trails need time Player feedback Jump, hit effects need to be seen Step-by-step tutorials Player needs to see each step

    repeat (height)

            add [platform] to [level-data v]
        else
            add [empty] to [level-data v]
        end
    end

docs.title: What Is Pseudocode?
docs.text: Pseudocode = writing your algorithm in plain English (or your language) before coding!

docs.title: Why Pseudocode?
docs.text: Benefit Explanation Think first Plan logic without syntax errors Share with team Non-coders can review Catch bugs early Logic errors caught before coding Language agnostic Works for any programming language

docs.title: Player Jump (Pseudocode)
docs.text:
WHEN green flag clicked:
    SET velocity-y to 0
    FOREVER:
        IF space pressed AND onGround:
            SET velocity-y to JUMP_POWER
        END IF

        // Apply gravity
        CHANGE velocity-y by GRAVITY

        // Move player
        CHANGE y by velocity-y

        // Ground check
        IF touching ground:
            SET velocity-y to 0
            SET onGround to TRUE
        ELSE:
            SET onGround to FALSE
        END IF
    END FOREVER

docs.title: Enemy Patrol (Pseudocode)
docs.text:
WHEN green flag clicked:
    FOREVER:
        MOVE forward 2 steps
        IF touching EDGE OR NOT touching ground:
            TURN 180 degrees
        END IF

        IF distance to PLAYER < 200:
            BROADCAST "chase-player"
        END IF
    END FOREVER

docs.title: Pseudocode → Scratch Blocks
docs.text: Pseudocode Scratch Blocks IF condition: if <condition> then ELSE: else END IF end FOREVER: forever REPEAT N times: repeat (N) SET var TO value: set [var] to (value) CHANGE var BY amount: change [var] by (amount) BROADCAST message: broadcast [message] WAIT seconds: wait (secs) secs

docs.title: Pseudocode Template
docs.text:
PROJECT: [Game Name]
GOAL: [What player does]

MAIN LOOP (when green flag clicked):
    SETUP: initialize variables, positions
    FOREVER:
        INPUT: check keys, sensors
        UPDATE: physics, AI, movement
        CHECK: collisions, win/lose
        RENDER: costumes, effects, UI
    END FOREVER

FUNCTIONS (custom blocks):
- define jump (height): ...
- define spawn-enemy (type): ...
- define check-collision (sprite): ...

docs.text: Predictable games get boring. Randomness = infinite replayability!

docs.title: Sources of Randomness
docs.text: Source Block Use For Random position pick random -200 to 200 Spawn locations Random timing pick random 1 to 5 Spawn intervals Random type pick random 1 to 3 Enemy variety Random reward pick random 1 to 100 Loot tables Random movement pick random -10 to 10 Wandering AI

docs.title: Controlled Randomness
docs.text:
Pure randomness can feel unfair. Control it!

Technique How Weighted random if <pick random 1 to 100 < 20> then rare else common Guaranteed drops if <kills = 10> then guaranteed rare Shuffle bag Fill list, shuffle, pull sequentially Pseudo-random seed Same seed = same sequence (for replays)

when green flag clicked
forever
    wait (pick random 1 to 3) secs
    create clone of [enemy v]
end

go to x: (pick random -200 to 200) y: 180
set [type v] to (pick random 1 to 3)  // 1=fast, 2=strong, 3=fast+strong

if < (roll) < 50 > then
    add [common-sword] to [inventory v]      // 50%
else
    if < (roll) < 80 > then
        add [uncommon-shield] to [inventory v]  // 30%
    else
        if < (roll) < 95 > then
            add [rare-potion] to [inventory v]   // 15%
        else

delete all of [level-data v]
repeat (20)    // 20 columns
    set [height v] to (pick random 2 to 8)
    repeat (height)
        add [block] to [level-data v]
    end
    repeat (10 - height)
        add [empty] to [level-data v]
    end
end

docs.title: What Is Error Detection?
docs.text: Error detection = code that notices when something's wrong and handles it!

docs.title: Common Error Types
docs.text: Error Type Example Detection Division by zero 10 / (score - score) Check denominator ≠ 0 List index out of range item (10) of [list] when length=5 Check length of list first Variable not initialized Using score before set score to 0 Check score exists Infinite loop forever without wait Add wait 0.01 secs Division by zero 10 / (x - x) Check denominator ≠ 0

docs.title: Check Before Divide
docs.text:
if < (denominator) = 0 > then
    set [result v] to (0)    // Or handle error
else
    set [result v] to ( (numerator) / (denominator) )
end

docs.title: Check List Bounds
docs.text:
if < (index) > (length of [list v]) > then
    say [Index out of range!] for 2 secs
else
    set [item v] to (item (index) of [list v])
end

docs.title: Initialize Variables
docs.text:
when green flag clicked
set [score v] to (0)        // ALWAYS initialize!
set [lives v] to (3)
set [level v] to (1)

docs.title: Error Detection in Game Loops
docs.text:
forever
    // Safe movement
    if < (x position) > 220 > then
        set x to 220
    end
    if < (x position) < -220 > then
        set x to -220
    end

    // Safe variable access
    if < (length of [inventory v]) > 0 > then
        // Safe to access items
    end
end

docs.title: Infinite Loop Detection — Stop the Freeze! ⚠️
What Causes Infinite Loops?
docs.text: Cause Example Fix forever without wait forever { change x by 1 } Add wait 0.01 secs repeat until never true repeat until <x > 100> but x never changes Ensure variable changes Recursive broadcast A broadcasts B, B broadcasts A Use flags to prevent cycles Clone explosion forever { create clone } no limit Add spawn limit/cooldown

docs.title: Infinite Loop Prevention
docs.text: Pattern Safe Version forever { move 10 } forever { move 10, wait 0.01 secs } repeat until <x > 100> { } Ensure x changes inside! forever { broadcast [A] } forever { broadcast [A], wait 1 secs }

docs.title: Infinite Loop Detection Script
docs.text:
when green flag clicked
forever
    if < (frame-count) > 10000 > then
        say [Possible infinite loop!] for 2 secs
        stop [all v]
    end
    change [frame-count v] by (1)
    wait 0.01 secs
end

Frame counter watchdog — stops project if too many frames!

switch costume to [mouth-closed v]

wait 2 secs

docs.title: Dialogue Timing Techniques
docs.text: Technique Code Speak and wait speak [Hello!] and wait Speak, pause, speak speak [Hi!] and wait, wait 1 secs, speak [How are you?] Character switching broadcast [char1-speak] and wait, broadcast [char2-speak] and wait Interrupt speak [Wait!] for 0.5 secs (short, urgent)

docs.text:
when I receive [start-dialogue v]
speak [Hello there, traveler!] and wait
wait 1 secs
speak [What brings you to our village?] and wait
wait 0.5 secs
broadcast [player-response v] and wait
speak [Ah, I see!] and wait
wait 0.5 secs
speak [Well, good luck on your journey!] and wait

docs.title: Natural Dialogue Tips
docs.text: Tip Code Vary pause length wait (pick random 0.5 to 1.5) secs Short for urgency speak [Run!] for 0.3 secs Long for thought wait 2 secs, speak [Hmm...] Overlap (advanced) speak [Hi] and wait + simultaneous broadcast [nod]

docs.text:
delete this clone

Removes the clone running this script — only works inside clone scripts!

docs.title: When to Delete Clones
docs.text: Situation Delete Code Off-screen if < (y position) < -200 > then delete this clone Hit something if <touching [player v]?> then delete this clone Lifetime expired wait 10 secs, delete this clone Reached target if <distance to [target] < 5> then delete this clone

point towards [player v]
forever

        delete this clone
    end

docs.text: Rule Explanation Only in clone scripts Won't work in original sprite scripts Stops script immediately Code after delete this clone won't run Original unaffected Only deletes the clone running it

docs.title: What Is Clone Behavior?
docs.text: Clone behavior = the logic that runs for each clone (via when I start as a clone).

docs.title: Clone Behavior Patterns
docs.text: Pattern Description Physics object Gravity, velocity, collision, delete on ground Particle Short life, fade out, stamp trail Enemy AI: patrol, chase, shoot, delete on death Projectile Move forward, delete on hit/wall Follower Follow leader with offset

docs.title: Clone Behavior Template
docs.text:
when I start as a clone
// 1. INITIALIZE
go to x: (random) y: (random)
set [velocity-x v] to (0)
set [velocity-y v] to (0)
switch costume to [default v]
show

// 2. MAIN LOOP
forever
    // PHYSICS
    change [velocity-y v] by (-0.5)   // Gravity
    change x by (velocity-x)
    change y by (velocity-y)

    // BEHAVIOR
    // ... specific to clone type ...

    // CLEANUP CHECKS
    if <touching [edge v]?> then
        delete this clone
    end
    if <touching [player v]?> then
        broadcast [player-hit v]
        delete this clone
    end
end

docs.title: Clone Behavior Types
docs.text: Type Key Behaviors Falling debris Gravity → delete on ground Particle Short life → fade → delete Projectile Move forward → delete on hit/wall Enemy AI → chase/patrol → delete on death Power-up Float → bob → delete on collect

docs.title: What Is an Event Queue?
docs.text: Event queue = the internal list of events waiting to be processed. Scratch processes events in order received.

docs.title: Event Processing Order
docs.text: Priority Event Type 1 Green flag (highest) 2 Key pressed / Sprite clicked 3 Broadcast received 4 Clone created 5 Video motion / Sensor events

docs.title: Event Queue Behavior
docs.text: Behavior Explanation FIFO First In, First Out — order received Broadcast and wait Pauses sender until ALL receivers done Async broadcast Sender continues, receivers queued Simultaneous events Processed in queue order

docs.title: Event Queue Example
docs.text:
when green flag clicked
broadcast [setup v] and wait    // Waits for ALL receivers
broadcast [spawn v] and wait    // Waits for ALL receivers  
broadcast [go v]                // Fire and forget

when I receive [setup v]
set [score v] to (0)

when I receive [spawn v]
create clone of [enemy v]

when I receive [go v]
forever
    // Game loop
end

Order: setup → spawn → go (sequential due to "and wait")

docs.title: Repeat Until Loop (Control → Orange)
docs.text:
repeat until <condition>
    // Runs until condition becomes TRUE
end

Checks condition at START of each iteration.

docs.title: Move Until Edge
docs.text:
repeat until <touching [edge v]?>
    move 5 steps
end

docs.title: Wait for Button
docs.text:
repeat until <key [space] pressed?>
    say [Press SPACE to start]
    wait 0.5 secs
end

docs.title: Chase Until Close
docs.text:
repeat until <distance to [target v] < 20>
    point towards [target v]
    move 3 steps
end

docs.title: Wait for Condition
docs.text:
repeat until < (score) > 100 >
    wait 1 secs
end
broadcast [level-complete v]

docs.title: Repeat Until vs Other Loops
docs.text: Loop Stops When... repeat (10) After exactly 10 times forever Never (manual stop) repeat until <cond> Condition becomes TRUE

docs.title: And Operator — Both Must Be True!
And Block (Operators → Green)
docs.text:
< <condition1> and <condition2> >

TRUE only if BOTH conditions are TRUE.

docs.title: Both Conditions Required
docs.text:
if <touching [coin v]?> and < (lives) > 0 > then
    change [score v] by (10)
end

docs.title: Multiple Safety Checks
docs.text:
if <key [space] pressed?> and <touching [ground v]?> then
    // Jump only if on ground AND space pressed
end

docs.title: Complex Conditions
docs.text:
if < (score) > 100 > and < (lives) > 0 > and <not <touching [spike v]?>> then
    broadcast [bonus-level v]
end

docs.text: A B A AND B T T T T F F F T F F F F

docs.title: Or Operator — At Least One True!
Or Block (Operators → Green)
docs.text:
< <condition1> or <condition2> >

TRUE if AT LEAST ONE condition is TRUE.

docs.title: Either Condition Works
docs.text:
if <touching [spike v]?> or <touching [lava v]?> then
    broadcast [player-hit v]
end

docs.title: Multiple Triggers
docs.text:
if <key [space] pressed?> or <key [w] pressed?> then
    // Jump with Space OR W
end

docs.title: Alternate Conditions
docs.text:
if <touching [enemy v]?> or < (lives) = 0 > then
    broadcast [game-over v]
end

docs.title: Or Truth Table
docs.text: A B A OR B T T T T F T F T T F F F

docs.title: Not Block (Operators → Green)
docs.text:
not <condition>

Flips TRUE ↔ FALSE.

docs.title: Invert Condition
docs.text:
if <not <touching [ground v]?>> then
    // In the air!
    change [velocity-y v] by (-1)   // Apply gravity
end

docs.title: Invert Sensor
docs.text:
if <not <key [space] pressed?>> then
    // Space NOT pressed
    set [running v] to (false)
end

docs.title: Double Negative (Avoid!)
docs.text:
if <not <not <touching [ground v]?>>> then
    // Confusing! Just use: touching ground?
end

docs.title: Not Truth Table
docs.text: A NOT A T F F T

docs.title: Lives Logic
docs.text:
when I receive [player-hit v]
if <not < (invincible) >> then
    change [lives v] by (-1)
    if < (lives) = 0 > then
        broadcast [game-over v]
    else
        set [invincible v] to (true)
        wait 2 secs
        set [invincible v] to (false)

end

forever
    set [minutes v] to ( (timer) / 60 )

docs.title: List Item Access — Getting Specific Items! 📋
List Item Block (Variables → Dark Red)
docs.text:
item (1) of [inventory v]

Reporter: gets the value at a specific position in the list.

docs.title: List Position Numbers
docs.text:
Lists are 1-indexed — first item is position 1, not 0!

Position Item 1 First item 2 Second item 3 Third item ... ... (length of list) Last item

docs.title: Access Specific Item
docs.text: say (item (1) of [inventory v]) for 2 secs  // Says first item

docs.title: Loop Through All Items
docs.text:
repeat (length of [inventory v])
    say (item (loop-counter) of [inventory v]) for 1 secs
end

docs.title: Get Last Item
docs.text: set [last-item v] to (item (length of [list v]) of [list v])

docs.title: List Item Safety
docs.text:
Always check bounds before accessing!

if < (index) > (length of [list v]) > then
    say [Invalid index!] for 2 secs
else
    say (item (index) of [list v]) for 2 secs
end

docs.title: Use Item from Inventory
docs.text:
when I receive [use-item v]
if < (length of [inventory v]) > 0 > then
    set [item-to-use v] to (item (1) of [inventory v])
    delete (1) of [inventory v]
    // Use the item...
end

docs.title: Equip Best Weapon
docs.text:
set [best-damage v] to (0)
repeat (length of [weapons v])
    if < (item (loop-counter) of [weapons v]) > (best-damage) > then
        set [best-damage v] to (item (loop-counter) of [weapons v])
        set [best-weapon-index v] to (loop-counter)
    end
end

docs.title: What Are Testing Strategies?
docs.text: Testing strategies = systematic ways to find bugs and verify your game works!

docs.title: Testing Levels
docs.text: Level What It Tests When Unit test Single script/block While coding Integration test Multiple scripts together After adding feature Playtest Full game experience Before sharing Regression test Old features still work After changes Edge case test Extreme/unusual inputs Before release

docs.title: Testing Strategies
docs.text: Strategy How To Do It Boundary testing Test edges: 0, 1, max, min, -1 Invalid input Wrong keys, empty lists, divide by 0 Stress test Spawn 100 clones, run 10 minutes Permutation test Try all key combinations Save/load test Save, reload, continue game Multiplayer test Two keyboards, two players

docs.title: Testing Checklist
docs.text: Category Tests Movement All directions, edges, collisions, jumping Controls All keys, key combos, rapid presses Physics Gravity, jumping, falling, slopes Combat Damage, knockback, invincibility, death Scoring Points, high scores, combos, multipliers Lives Lose, gain, game over, invincibility Levels Transitions, spawns, completion, secrets UI Menus, pause, menus, displays Audio Music, SFX, volume, mute Performance 100 clones, 10 min play, save/load

docs.title: Automated Testing (Custom Blocks)
docs.text:
define test-movement
// Test: Player moves right
go to x: 0 y: 0
repeat 10
    change x by 5
end
if < (x position) = 50 > then
    say [TEST PASS: Movement] for 2 secs
else
    say [TEST FAIL: Movement] for 2 secs
end

define test-collision
// Test: Wall collision
go to x: 220 y: 0
if <touching color [#FF0000]? > then
    say [TEST PASS: Collision] for 2 secs
else
    say [TEST FAIL: Collision] for 2 secs
end

docs.title: Debugging Strategies — Fix Bugs Like a Pro! 🐛
Debugging Workflow
docs.text:
1. REPRODUCE → Make bug happen every time
2. ISOLATE → Which script? Which block?
3. HYPOTHESIZE → "I think the 'change x by' is wrong"
4. TEST → Change ONE thing, test again
5. FIX → Apply correction
6. VERIFY → Test thoroughly, check for new bugs

docs.title: Debugging Tools in Scratch
docs.text: Tool How to Use Block Highlighting Watch which block glows during execution Variable Watchers show variable — see values live on stage say Debugging say (variable) for 0.1 secs — live values wait for Timing wait 1 secs to slow down and observe Single Step Some Scratch versions: step through blocks Clean Up Right-click → "Clean up" — aligns blocks

docs.title: Debugging with say (Live Values!)
docs.text:
forever
    say (join [x: ] (x position)) for 0.1 secs
    say (join [y: ] (y position)) for 0.1 secs
    say (join [vel-x: ] (velocity-x)) for 0.1 secs
    say (join [onGround: ] (touching [ground v]?)) for 0.1 secs
    wait 0.1 secs
end

Live dashboard of all important values! 📊

docs.title: Common Bug Patterns & Fixes
docs.text: Bug Symptom Likely Cause Debug Steps Sprite frozen forever without wait Add wait 0.01 secs Moves wrong way Wrong sign (+/-) Check change x by sign Jumps infinitely No ground check Add touching ground? Stuck in wall No collision check Add touching color? Score not updating Wrong variable name Check score vs Score Clone explosion No spawn limit Add cooldown/limit Lag/freeze Too many loops Combine loops, add wait

docs.title: Debugging Strategies
docs.text: Strategy How To Apply Divide and conquer Disable half the code, test, narrow down Rubber duck debugging Explain code to a rubber duck (or friend) Binary search Disable half scripts, test, narrow to one script Minimal reproduction Create new project with just the buggy part Print everything say all variables at each step Check assumptions "Is this variable actually 0?" — verify with say

docs.title: Storytelling Flow — Games That Tell Stories! 📖
What Is Storytelling Flow?
docs.text: Storytelling flow = how your game guides the player through a narrative experience!

docs.title: Story Structure in Games
docs.text: Act Purpose Game Elements Setup (Act 1) Introduce world, character, goal Tutorial, first level, intro cutscene Confrontation (Act 2) Challenges, rising action Harder levels, new mechanics, mid-boss Climax (Act 3) Final challenge, resolution Final boss, final level, ending cutscene

docs.title: Storytelling Through Gameplay
docs.text: Story Element Game Mechanic Character Player sprite, customization Setting Backdrops, level design Conflict Enemies, obstacles, puzzles Progression Levels, upgrades, new abilities Resolution Win screen, credits, epilogue

docs.title: Storytelling Through Code
docs.text:
when green flag clicked
broadcast [chapter1 v] and wait    // Setup
broadcast [chapter2 v] and wait    // Rising action
broadcast [chapter3 v] and wait    // Climax
broadcast [ending v]               // Resolution

when I receive [chapter1 v]
switch backdrop to [village v]
speak [Our village was peaceful...] and wait
speak [Until the Shadow King came...] and wait
broadcast [chapter1-done v]

when I receive [chapter2 v]
switch backdrop to [forest v]
speak [You must find the three crystals...] and wait
// Gameplay: collect 3 crystals

docs.title: Broadcast And Wait Recap
docs.text:
broadcast [message v] and wait

Pauses sender until ALL when I receive scripts FINISH.

docs.title: When to Use Synchronous Broadcast
docs.text: Scenario Why Sync Level start All sprites initialized before gameplay Cutscene steps Each line finishes before next Save game All data saved before continuing Multi-phase boss Phase 1 done before phase 2 starts Cutscene dialogue Each character finishes speaking

docs.title: Synchronous Broadcast Example
docs.text:
when green flag clicked
broadcast [initialize v] and wait
wait 1 secs
broadcast [spawn-player v] and wait
broadcast [spawn-enemies v] and wait
broadcast [spawn-ui v] and wait
broadcast [game-ready v]

when I receive [initialize v]
set [score v] to (0)
set [lives v] to (3)

when I receive [spawn-player v]
go to x: -200 y: -100
show

when I receive [spawn-enemies v]
repeat 5
    create clone of [enemy v]
    wait 0.2 secs
end

docs.title: What Is a Broadcast Storm?
docs.text: Broadcast storm = too many broadcasts sent too quickly = lag, crashes, unpredictable behavior!

docs.title: Causes of Broadcast Storms
docs.text: Cause Example Broadcast in forever loop forever { broadcast [update] } Recursive broadcasts A → B, B → A, A → B... Too many clones broadcasting 100 clones each broadcast Broadcast in when I receive Chain reaction

docs.title: Preventing Broadcast Storms
docs.text: Prevention How Rate limit wait 0.1 secs between broadcasts Flags if <not <broadcasting>> then broadcast Cooldown set [cooldown v] to (10), change by -1 each frame Single broadcaster One "manager" sprite handles all broadcasts

docs.title: Broadcast Storm Example (BAD!)
docs.text:
forever
    broadcast [update v]    // STORM! Thousands per second
end

docs.title: Broadcast Storm Fix (GOOD!)
docs.text:
forever
    broadcast [update v]
    wait 0.1 secs   // Rate limited!
end

docs.title: How Loops End
docs.text: Loop Type Terminates When... repeat (N) After N iterations forever stop [this script] or stop [all] repeat until <cond> Condition becomes TRUE repeat while (custom) Condition becomes FALSE

docs.title: Loop Termination Blocks
docs.text: Block Stops stop [this script v] Current script only stop [all v] EVERYTHING in project stop [other scripts in sprite v] Other scripts in same sprite

docs.title: Break Out of Forever
docs.text:
forever
    if <key [escape] pressed?> then
        stop [this script v]
    end
    // Game loop code
end

docs.title: Exit Nested Loop
docs.text:
repeat (10)
    repeat (10)
        if <touching [target v]?> then
            stop [this script v]  // Exits BOTH loops!
        end
    end
end

docs.title: Stop All (Game Over)
docs.text:
when I receive [game-over v]
stop [all v]

docs.title: Loop Termination Best Practices
docs.text: Practice Why Always have exit condition forever must have stop or broadcast [stop] Use stop [this script] Prefer over stop [all] Clean up before stop hide, delete this clone, stop sounds Avoid stop [all] in libraries Kills everything including UI

docs.title: Combining Booleans (And/Or/Not)
docs.text: Operator Block True When... AND < > and < > BOTH true OR < > or < > AT LEAST ONE true NOT not < > Flips true/false

docs.title: Three Conditions (AND)
docs.text:
if < (score) > 100 > and < (lives) > 0 > and <not <touching [spike v]?>> then
    broadcast [bonus-level v]
end

docs.title: Complex Condition
docs.text:
if < < (distance) < 50 > or <touching [player v]?> > and <not < (invincible) >> then
    broadcast [player-hit v]
end

docs.title: De Morgan's Laws (Simplify!)
docs.text: Original Equivalent (Simplified) not (A or B) (not A) and (not B) not (A and B) (not A) or (not B)

docs.title: Complex Jump Condition
docs.text:
if <key [space] pressed?> and <touching [ground v]?> and <not < (in-air) >> then
    set [velocity-y v] to (15)
end

docs.title: Enemy AI Decision
docs.text:
if < (distance to player) < 100 > and <not < (stunned) >> then
    if < (player-x) > (x position) > then
        set [velocity-x v] to (3)
    else
        set [velocity-x v] to (-3)
    end
end

docs.title: What Is a Win Condition?
docs.text: Win condition = the specific goal that makes the player win the game!

docs.title: Common Win Conditions
docs.text: Type Condition Example Score target score > 1000 Collect 100 coins All collected length of [coins] = 0 Get all items Reach location x > 200 and y > 150 Reach exit Defeat boss boss-health = 0 Defeat final boss Survive time timer > 300 Survive 5 minutes All enemies gone length of [enemies] = 0 Clear room

docs.title: Win Condition Implementation
docs.text:
forever
    // Check win conditions each frame
    if < (score) > 1000 > then
        broadcast [win v]
        stop [this script v]
    end

    if < (length of [coins v]) = 0 > then
        broadcast [win v]
        stop [this script v]
    end

    if < (boss-health) = 0 > then
        broadcast [win v]
        stop [this script v]
    end
end

docs.title: Win Sequence
docs.text:
when I receive [win v]
stop [all v]
switch backdrop to [victory v]
play sound [fanfare v]
say [YOU WIN!] for 5 secs
wait 3 secs
show variable [final-score v]
wait 5 secs
broadcast [return-to-menu v]

docs.title: Multiple Win Paths
docs.text: Game Type Win Conditions Platformer Reach flag, all coins, defeat boss Puzzle All pieces placed, all switches hit Survival Timer reaches target RPG Defeat final boss, complete main quest Racing Cross finish line first

docs.title: What Is a Lose Condition?
docs.text: Lose condition = specific situation where the player fails and game ends!

docs.title: Common Lose Conditions
docs.text: Type Condition Example No lives lives = 0 3 hits = game over Time out timer = 0 Didn't finish in time Fall off world y < -200 Fell in pit Touch hazard touching lava/spikes Instant death Fail objective failed to protect NPC Escort mission failed

docs.title: Lose Condition Implementation
docs.text:
forever
    // Check lose conditions
    if < (lives) = 0 > then
        broadcast [game-over v]
        stop [this script v]
    end

    if < (timer) = 0 > then
        broadcast [game-over v]
        stop [this script v]
    end

    if < (y position) < -200 > then
        broadcast [game-over v]
        stop [this script v]
    end

    if <touching [lava v]?> then
        broadcast [game-over v]
        stop [this script v]
    end
end

docs.title: Game Over Sequence
docs.text:
when I receive [game-over v]
stop [all v]
switch backdrop to [game-over v]
play sound [game-over-sound v]
say [GAME OVER] for 3 secs
wait 2 secs
say (join [Final Score: ] (score)) for 5 secs
wait 3 secs
broadcast [return-to-menu v]

docs.title: Lose Condition Best Practices
docs.text: Practice Why Clear feedback Show WHY player lost Quick restart One click to try again Progress saving Don't lose all progress Fair warning "Low health!" before death Learn from failure Show what killed you

docs.title: What Is an Inventory System?
docs.text: Inventory = a list that holds items the player collects!

docs.title: Inventory List Structure
docs.text:
inventory list:
[0] "health-potion"
[1] "iron-sword"
[2] "gold-key"
[3] "magic-scroll"

docs.title: Inventory Operations
docs.text: Operation Code Add item add [potion] to [inventory v] Remove item delete (1) of [inventory v] Use item item (1) of [inventory v], then delete (1) Check item [potion] in [inventory v]? Count items length of [inventory v] Show inventory show list [inventory v]

docs.title: Simple Inventory (Stack)
docs.text:
when I receive [pickup-item v]
add [item-name] to [inventory v]
say (join [Got: ] (item-name)) for 2 secs

docs.title: Categorized Inventory
docs.text:
Categories: weapons, potions, keys, quest

when I receive [pickup v]
if < (item-type) = [weapon] > then
    add (item) to [weapons v]
else
    if < (item-type) = [potion] > then
        add (item) to [potions v]
    end
end

docs.title: Weight/Slot Limit
docs.text:
if < (length of [inventory v]) < 20 > then
    add [item] to [inventory v]
else
    say [Inventory full!] for 2 secs
end

docs.title: Inventory UI
docs.text:
when green flag clicked
hide list [inventory v]

when [i] key pressed
if < (showing-inventory) > then
    hide list [inventory v]
    set [showing-inventory v] to (false)
else
    show list [inventory v]
    set [showing-inventory v] to (true)
end

docs.title: The Design Process — Your Creative Roadmap! 🗺️
What Is the Design Process?
docs.text: The Design Process = a step-by-step method for turning ideas into finished projects. Professional game developers, engineers, artists, and inventors ALL use it!

docs.title: The 6 Stages
docs.text:
IMAGINE → PLAN → CREATE → TEST → IMPROVE → SHARE
     ↑_____________REFLECT_____________↓

Reflection happens at EVERY stage! 🔄

docs.title: What Is Imagine?
docs.text: Imagine = let your creativity run wild! No limits, no "that's impossible" — just pure ideas!

docs.title: Imagine Activities
docs.text: Activity Description Brainstorm Write 20 game ideas in 5 minutes Mind Map Central idea → branches of features Mashup Combine two games: "Mario + Tetris" What If? "What if gravity reversed?" "What if you played as the villain?" Inspiration Board Collect images, colors, music that inspire you

docs.title: Imagine Questions
docs.text: Question Purpose What's the core fun? What makes the player smile? Who is the player? Kid, teen, adult, family? What's the hook? Why keep playing after 5 minutes? What's unique? What makes YOUR game special? What's the feeling? Joy, tension, wonder, mastery?

docs.title: Imagine Output
docs.text:
One-sentence Game Concept:

"A [genre] game where you [core action] to [goal] while [challenge], featuring [unique twist]."

Example:

"A platformer where you dash through time to collect chrono-shards while avoiding paradox monsters, featuring past/future world switching."

docs.title: What Is Plan?
docs.text: Plan = turn your wild idea into a buildable blueprint with clear steps!

docs.title: Plan Deliverables
docs.text: Document Purpose Game Design Document (GDD) Complete game specification Storyboard Visual scene-by-scene plan Asset List Every sprite, sound, backdrop needed Flowchart Logic flow for complex systems Task List Ordered steps with priorities Milestones Checkpoints: v0.1, v1.0, v2.0...

docs.title: Game Design Document (GDD) Template
docs.text:
GAME DESIGN DOCUMENT
====================
Title: [Game Name]
Genre: [Platformer/Puzzle/RPG/etc.]
Target Audience: [Ages 8-12 / All Ages]
Core Mechanic: [One-sentence description]
Win Condition: [How to win]
Lose Condition: [How to lose]
Controls: [Key mappings]
Levels: [Number, themes, progression]
Sprites: [Player, enemies, items, UI]
Sounds: [Music, SFX, voice]
Extensions: [Pen, Video, micro:bit, etc.]
Milestones:
  v0.1 - Core movement
  v0.5 - First playable level
  v1.0 - Complete game
  v1.1 - Polish & bug fixes

docs.title: Storyboard — Visual Script! 🎬
docs.text:
Storyboard = comic-strip style plan of your game's scenes!

Panel What to Draw Notes 1 Title screen "Press SPACE to start" 2 Level 1 start "Tutorial: Move with arrows" 3 First challenge "Jump over spikes" 4 First reward "Coin gives 10 points" 5 Mid-level twist "New enemy type appears" 6 Level complete "All coins collected!" 7 Level 2 start "New mechanic: Double jump" ... ... ... Final Victory screen "YOU WIN! Final score: ___"

docs.title: Asset List — Shopping List! 🛒
docs.text: Category Assets Needed Sprites Player (idle, walk1-4, jump), Enemy1, Enemy2, Coin, Spike, Platform, UI hearts Backdrops Title, Level1, Level2, Boss, GameOver, Victory Sounds Jump, Coin, Hit, Music-L1, Music-L2, GameOver, Victory Costumes Player idle, walk1-4, jump, hurt; Enemy walk1-2, hurt UI Score display, Lives hearts, Timer, Pause menu

docs.title: Flowchart — Logic Map! 🗺️
docs.text:
START → Initialize Variables → MAIN LOOP
                    ↓
            Check Input (Keys)
                    ↓
            Update Physics (Gravity, Velocity)
                    ↓
            Check Collisions (Ground, Enemies, Coins)
                    ↓
            Update Animations
                    ↓
            Check Win/Lose
                    ↓
            Update UI
                    ↓
            WAIT 0.01s → LOOP

docs.title: Task List — Prioritized Steps!
docs.text: Priority Task Milestone 🔴 Critical Player movement (left/right/jump) v0.1 🔴 Critical Ground collision v0.1 🔴 Critical Camera follow v0.1 🟡 High Coin collection + score v0.2 🟡 High Enemy patrol AI v0.2 🟡 High Level design (3 levels) v0.5 🟢 Medium Boss fight v0.8 🟢 Medium Sound effects + music v0.9 🔵 Low Particle effects v1.0 🔵 Low Unlockable skins v1.1

docs.title: What Is Create?
docs.text: Create = write the code, draw the art, record the sounds — make it real!

docs.title: Create Best Practices
docs.text: Practice Why One thing at a time Build movement, test, THEN add coins Test constantly Run after EVERY change Use versioning Save v0.1, v0.2, v0.3... Comment your code Future you will thank you Clean up regularly Right-click → Clean up

docs.title: Create Order (Suggested)
docs.text:
1. Core movement (player controller)
  2. Camera follow (if scrolling)
  3. Ground collision (platforms)
  4. Collectibles (coins, score)
  5. Enemies (patrol, chase)
  6. Hazards (spikes, lava)
  7. Lives/Game Over (health system)
  8. Level transitions (broadcasts)
  9. UI (score, lives, timer)
  10. Sound effects (jump, coin, hit)
  11. Music (level themes)
  12. Polish (particles, juice, menus)

docs.title: What Is Test?
docs.text: Test = systematically verify every feature works and find bugs!

docs.title: Test Phases
docs.text: Phase Focus Who Self-test You play your own game You Target audience test Kids play your game Friends/siblings Stress test Push limits (100 clones, 30 min) You Edge case test Weird inputs, rapid clicks You Regression test Old features after changes You

docs.title: Test Checklist
docs.text: Category Specific Tests Movement All directions, speeds, jumping, edges Collision Ground, walls, ceilings, slopes, enemies Collectibles Score adds, sound plays, item disappears Enemies Patrol, chase, damage, defeat Hazards Spikes, lava, pits, falling Lives Lose life, invincibility, game over Levels Transitions, spawns, completion UI Score, lives, timer, menus, pause Audio Music loops, SFX volume, mute Performance 100 clones, 30 min, save/load

docs.title: Test Documentation
docs.text:
TEST LOG - v0.5
===============
Date: 2026-06-10
Tester: Me

PASSED:
✅ Player moves left/right smoothly
✅ Jump works from ground only
✅ Coin collection adds 10 points
✅ Enemy patrol turns at edges

FAILED:
❌ Player gets stuck in wall corner
❌ Enemy sometimes walks through platform
❌ Music doesn't loop properly

NOTES:
- Wall sticking: need better corner collision
- Enemy: check ground detection
- Music: check loop points

docs.title: What Is Improve?
docs.text: Improve = fix bugs, add polish, balance difficulty, add "juice"!

docs.title: Improvement Categories
docs.text: Category Examples Bug Fixes Wall sticking, enemy clipping, music loops Balance Enemy speed, jump height, coin values Juice Screen shake, particle effects, screen flash Accessibility Colorblind mode, adjustable speed Quality of Life Checkpoints, level select, skip cutscene Performance Reduce clones, optimize loops

docs.title: The "Juice" Checklist 🍹
docs.text: Juice Element Implementation Impact Screen shake change x by (pick random -5 to 5) on hit Impact feel Screen flash change color effect by 50, wait, clear Damage feedback Particle burst Clones + stamp + fade on collect/hit Satisfaction Sound variation pick random pitch on repeated SFX Less repetition Screen pause wait 0.05 secs on big events Weight/impact Coyote time Allow jump 0.1s after leaving ground Forgiving jumps Jump buffering Queue jump if pressed slightly early Responsive feel

docs.title: Balancing Difficulty
docs.text: Too Easy Too Hard Just Right Enemies never hit Instant death traps Fair challenge Infinite lives One-hit kills 3 lives + checkpoints No time pressure Impossible time limits Generous but present Boring repetition Impossible jumps Variety + progression

docs.title: Iterative Development — Cycle Until Perfect! 🔄
docs.text:
PLAN → CREATE → TEST → IMPROVE → TEST → IMPROVE → TEST...

Each cycle makes the game better! Most pro games go through 50+ iterations.

docs.title: What Is Share?
docs.text: Share = publish your game so others can play, enjoy, and remix!

docs.title: Before Sharing Checklist
docs.text: ✅ Ready to Share? Check No game-breaking bugs Played 10 min without crash Clear instructions "Arrows move, Space jumps" Credits included Art, music, code sources Tags added "platformer, pixel-art, fun" Thumbnail set Eye-catching project image Notes complete Changelog, controls, credits

docs.title: Sharing Steps
docs.text:
1. Click Share (📤) in toolbar
  2. Add clear title: "Super Coin Collector v1.2"
  3. Write instructions: "Arrows move, Space jumps, Collect all coins!"
  4. Add credits: "Music by Kevin MacLeod. Art by me."
  5. Add tags: "platformer, pixel-art, coin-collector, fun"
  6. Choose visibility: Anyone / Link only / Private
  7. Click Share!

docs.title: After Sharing
docs.text: Action Why Send to friends Get first players Post in studios "Cool Platformers" studio Ask for feedback "What's too hard/easy?" Watch remixes See how others extend your game Respond to comments Build community Update based on feedback v1.1, v1.2, v1.3...

docs.title: Sound Design Tips
docs.text: Tip Why Pitch variation change pitch by (pick random -10 to 10) — less repetitive Layer sounds Jump + land = two sounds = more impact Volume balance Music quieter than SFX Silence is powerful Pause music for tension Test on phone speaker Many kids play on tablets

docs.title: What Is "Juice"?
docs.text: Juice = visual/audio feedback that makes actions feel satisfying, powerful, alive!

docs.title: Juice Techniques
docs.text: Technique Code Effect Screen shake repeat 5: change x by (pick random -5 to 5), wait 0.02, end Impact Screen flash change color effect by 50, wait 0.05, clear graphic effects Hit flash Scale pop set size to 120%, wait 0.05, set size to 100% Bounce feel Color flash change color effect by 50, wait 0.05, clear Damage/collect Particles Clones + stamp + change ghost by 5 + delete Explosion Screen pause wait 0.05 secs on big events Weight Trail effect pen down on fast movement Speed feel

docs.title: What Is Reflection?
docs.text: Reflection = looking back at your project to learn what worked, what didn't, and how to improve next time!

docs.title: Reflection Questions
docs.text: Question Purpose What am I most proud of? Celebrate success What was hardest? Identify learning gaps What would I do differently? Improve process What did I learn? Cement knowledge What's next? Plan future projects

docs.title: Reflection Template
docs.text:
PROJECT REFLECTION
==================
Game: [Name]
Version: [v1.2]
Date Completed: [Date]

WHAT WENT WELL:
- Smooth player movement felt great
- Enemy AI was challenging but fair
- Juice effects made collecting coins satisfying
- Music fit the theme perfectly

CHALLENGES OVERCOME:
- Wall sticking bug → fixed with raycast collision
- Enemy AI too aggressive → tuned detection radius
- Music looping click → fixed with seamless loop points

WHAT I LEARNED:
- Broadcast and wait is essential for level loading
- Variable scope (global vs local) matters a lot
- Juice effects make huge difference in feel
- Testing with actual kids reveals real issues

NEXT TIME I'LL:
- Plan asset list more carefully upfront
- Use versioning from day 1 (lost v0.3!)
- Add automated tests for core mechanics
- Design juice effects earlier in process

NEXT PROJECT IDEAS:
- Metroidvania with map system
- Multiplayer co-op platformer
- Level editor for players
